key_insight: This paper shows that a welding penetration classifier can be transferred across very different welding processes without labels in the target process by using unsupervised domain adaptation. Its gradual source domain expansion strategy helps bridge the gap between TIG and laser welding, where the physics and signal patterns differ strongly.
problem_solved: It addresses the drop in deep-learning performance caused by domain shift when a model trained on one welding process, such as TIG, is applied to another, such as laser welding, without target labels.
method: Uses an unsupervised domain adaptation framework to learn transferable features from a labeled source process and unlabeled target process.
Introduces gradual source domain expansion (GSDE) to progressively broaden the source knowledge and reduce the mismatch between welding domains.
Targets cross-process weld penetration status prediction across welding types with distinct physical mechanisms.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this demonstrates a practical way to deploy models in new industrial settings where labels are scarce or unavailable. It is especially relevant for robust transfer learning under strong real-world domain shifts.

paper_title: A cross-process welding penetration status prediction algorithm based on unsupervised domain adaptation in laser and TIG welding
